last_judge_summary:
Not done. Most of the work holds up. The full suite passes (161 OK), migrations are clean, and seed_load and benchmark both run. CAPACITY.md has the before and after table. The subquery rewrite of the audience checks, the thread caps, the grouped counts, list_select_related in the admin and migration 0007 are sound, and the challenger's randomised check found no visibility leak.

Three objections stand, and each needs a small change:
1. Replies per thread are still unbounded on the feed and the post page (C1/S1). I reproduced it: with 5 vs 200 replies on a pinned post, the feed drew every reply and went from 39 KB to 642 KB, with flat query counts. That contradicts CAPACITY.md's claim and the mission's "fix unbounded lists".
2. CAPACITY.md tells operators to run seed_load on the test server (S2/C7/C8). That breaks handover's rule against made-up people on the test hub, sets off the nightly leaver-check alarm, and sends digest emails to the fake accounts. The guard also doesn't stop a live hub that has staff but no posts.
3. The psql -U hub steps break once hardening's NOSUPERUSER roles land (C3), and the stuck-query check then fails silently.

Minor items that may stay open: C4 (Referer), C5 (gunicorn has no access log), C6 (the rush estimate leaves out media requests and misreads burst), S3 (?comments=all has no ceiling), S4 (slow-query logs would hold session keys; prefer pg_stat_statements), S5 (benchmark admin rows return 403 unless /admin/ ranges are widened). The builder's own open items also remain: nothing measured on Postgres, template rendering cost, and the group page's double decorate.

Blueprint checks: none fully completed. 08-load-and-flood-testing has moved forward for data volume, but nothing sends request floods or concurrent spikes. 15-scale-without-weakening-security is not met by this branch, since it adds no caches or replicas.

last_build.summary: Round 2 of team performance: all three required fixes are done. The full suite passes: "Ran 163 tests ... OK" with --parallel 2. makemigrations --check reports no changes, and the branch merges cleanly with all nine wave-1 branches (checked with git merge-tree). (1) Each comment thread now loads only its newest replies: 3 on a card, 20 on the post page, and all of them with ?comments=all. This uses a sliced Prefetch with to_attr="newest_replies", and the replies are shown oldest first. A "View N more replies" link uses per-thread reply counts, which now come from decorate's existing grouped query, grouped by (post_id, parent_id), so the query count doesn't change. Re-measured on the same data, the feed went from 3.2 MB and 3236 ms before this work to 412 KB and 400 ms now. Round 1's thread cap alone still gave 3.2 MB and 1984 ms. seed_load now builds a thread of 60 to 200 replies under the newest thread of every pinned post, so the benchmark measures long threads. To make that work, after() no longer caps late comments at exactly now: that capping gave the newest threads all the same time, so the feed never showed the long ones. (2) seed_load refuses any database that has an account, and its made-up staff have email_digest=False. CAPACITY.md now has the Postgres measurement run on a spare machine or VM as its own compose project (-p hub-load), with its own volumes, no scheduler, no Entra or email settings and a dummy email backend, and thrown away with down -v. It says never the test hub or the live hub. (3) Every psql line uses `docker compose exec db psql -U postgres hub`, with a note to use -U hub on a server installed before hardening. The stuck-query check says it must run as postgres. I also did four of the minor items: S4, by replacing the slow-query log recipe with pg_stat_statements (one flag in the db command I already own in docker-compose.yml); S5; C5; and C6.
open_items: Nothing has been measured on Postgres. Docker isn't on this PC, so the hub-load compose steps, `psql -U postgres` working inside the db container, pg_stat_statements loading from the postgres:17 image, and the replies prefetch on Postgres (window function over the parent index) were checked only by reading. The YAML was parsed with pyyaml.
?comments=all still has no ceiling or paging (S3, accepted as minor). It now also shows every reply, which is the point of that view.
The grouped count now returns one row per thread that has replies (a few hundred for the busiest posts). It is cheap here, but on Postgres it should be watched with pg_stat_statements.
Template rendering is now most of the feed's cost (about 16 ms and 16 KB per card: reaction forms, icon ifs). Not changed.
The group page's double decorate is left until QA's change merges, as in round 1.
Rush figures are estimates. Nothing sends real request floods or concurrent spikes yet, so 08-load-and-flood-testing is only partly covered.

I haven't run a merged suite with team/experience's a11y tests or team/redteam's ceilings. git merge-tree shows no textual conflicts, and my change adds no queries, so their ceilings should still hold.
